title: Recoloured body sheet cache: lazy bake, bounded retry, later rounds, drawing drop
oneLine: Per-look recoloured body sheets: absent, loading, baked, given up, later round, dropped on a drawing edit.
topConcern: buildBodySheet's retry is not chained into its promise, so the loading screen passes with a facing on backoff; drops race in-flight bakes.

title: Head-overlay sheet cache with its 32-sheet cap
oneLine: Pickup/jog/hit/mine head sheets per skin, eye style and face drawing, capped at 32 with local-player protection.
topConcern: The cap's local-combo guard still includes trousers/boots that the head key dropped (v2.3.3658), so non-default dressers' own heads are evicted first.

title: Gear sheet cache with chained retry, later rounds and the drawn-shirt LRU
oneLine: Gear and dressed-tee sheets: absent, loading, loaded, given up, later round; dressings evicted by an 8-key LRU.
topConcern: Nine dressings on screen cascade the LRU: every frame evicts and rebuilds every dressed tee, releasing sources a sprite is still drawing.

title: The worn armour layer: derived from stat pieces but still written by cosmetic paths
oneLine: Per-slot drawn armour layer in localStorage, meant to mirror the server's worn stat pieces.
topConcern: InventoryPanel's Legs Unequip always takes the cosmetic path: art off, stat greaves still worn and mitigating, a costume duplicate saved.

title: Local look stores and the prewarms their changes trigger
oneLine: Skin/trousers/boots stores in localStorage, each change prewarming the stand sheets of the new combo.
topConcern: Eye colour is in the sheet key but triggers no prewarm; a batch look change bakes every intermediate combo and never frees them.

title: The look palette: sets, program link, and each look's atlas row
oneLine: Colour-number sheet sets, the shader program per renderer, and per-look palette rows swept after 30 s idle.
topConcern: A set that fails once is never retried, so phones draw copies for the visit; a failed set can end half-present.

title: Body under armour from the numbers: per-frame decided states, books, mask atlas
oneLine: Per (look, worn set, sheet) frame states undecided/asked/decided via worker jobs, plus masked-look rows and books.
topConcern: A failed frame (beltPending, gear not loaded) goes back to undecided and is re-asked every draw with no backoff.

title: Dressed tee from the numbers: dressings cache, live switch, fallback chain
oneLine: Tee dressings as palette row entries, FIFO-capped, falling back to the old dressed copy.

title: Townsfolk drawn live or from photographs
oneLine: Load-time and per-frame decisions on drawing townsfolk from looks or photographs, with a late photo load.

title: Character portrait: per-canvas draw sequence and never-expiring promise caches
oneLine: Portrait asset promise caches (kept forever, rejections included) and a per-canvas stale-draw counter.
topConcern: A flaked body or trait image stays a cached rejection for the visit; the body layer has no catch, so that facing's portraits fail.

title: Hemi Bro headshot: page choice, atlas load, data-URL LRU
oneLine: Dormant Hemi Bro headshot pipeline behind ?hemiface=1: atlas load with retry and a 24-entry cache.

title: Look oracles and the pipeline's QA probes
oneLine: QA-only probes polling the caches until bakes land and comparing old and new look paths texel for texel.

title: Role bake mirror: offline colour numbers vs the live recolour
oneLine: Baked look sheets must match the live recolour code; precheck fails art changes but only warns on code changes.
topConcern: A recolour-rule change only WARNS, so phones (numbers) and computers (live) can ship drawing the same look differently.

title: Base body sheets: load once, chained retry, later rounds
oneLine: Shipped body sheet manifest per pose and facing, with awaited retries and later rounds while drawn.

title: One-shot loaders with no later round: hand anchors, weapon grips, death strip
oneLine: anchors.json/handles.json and the death strip load once; a failure keeps the fallback for the visit.
topConcern: A flaked anchors fetch leaves every weapon at the legacy four-way offset, out of the hand, for the whole session.
